subject.title: feat(agents): per-agent outbound A2A allowlist override

question: Should OpenClaw accept an outbound-only `agents.list[].tools.agentToAgent.allow` config shape as a narrow A2A authorization slice before the broader per-agent/per-capability session visibility design is settled?
rationale: The implementation is plausible and well-proven, but it changes a public cross-agent authorization boundary and overlaps open product/security design threads, so automation cannot choose the permanent config semantics safely.

options.title: Accept after repairs
options.body: Fix the exact-entry normalization issue, remove the manual changelog edit, resolve conflicts, and land the outbound-only A2A slice with explicit maintainer signoff.

options.title: Fold into broader design
options.body: Pause this PR and carry the useful policy/test work into the canonical per-agent session visibility and A2A scoping design in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/59149.

options.title: Reject this config shape
options.body: Close or supersede the PR if maintainers want cross-agent authorization solved only through a unified per-capability visibility model.

recommendation.title: Accept after repairs
recommendation.body: Fix the exact-entry normalization issue, remove the manual changelog edit, resolve conflicts, and land the outbound-only A2A slice with explicit maintainer signoff.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest history on the A2A allowlist security surface and is already tied to the canonical session authorization decision path.
